# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who can hear whom and who can see whom.

- I (Mute) can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures.
- Blind cannot see gestures or read anything printed, but can hear speech.
- Deaf can see gestures and see the bomb, but cannot hear speech.

So I cannot communicate directly with Blind at all — I have no channel to them (Blind can't see my gestures, and I can't speak). I must route my information through Deaf, who sees my gestures, and then Deaf must speak the info to Blind (since Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear).

The manual says: cut purple, then blue, then green.

I need a gesture code for colors that Deaf will understand and then relay verbally to Blind. Since it's turn 1 and Deaf hasn't sent anything yet, I should establish a simple mapping now. I'll pick distinct gesture symbols for purple, blue, green, and an ordering convention.

Let me assign: ☝ = first, ✌ = second, 🤟 = third (order markers), and 👍=purple, 👎=blue, 👌=green (color markers). I'll gesture the sequence pairing order with color.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: keypad shows four slots with engraved digits: slot1 is 8, slot2 is 1, slot3 is 5, slot4 is 3. it wants 1 digit entered, nothing entered yet. strip has three engraved marks, i cannot read their shapes meaningfully, first looks different from the other two which look same to touch. six wires present, no info yet on which to cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Let me analyze this new information from Blind.

Blind says: keypad has 4 slots with digits 8,1,5,3 (engraved, feelable), wants 1 digit entered. Also a strip with three engraved marks - first is different, other two feel the same. Six wires present.

My manual only covers wires (purple, blue, green order) - nothing about a keypad or a strip with marks. This suggests Deaf may see additional info on the bomb about the keypad (maybe a highlighted digit or marking indicating which digit to press), and the strip likely corresponds to my wire-cutting instructions somehow (three marks = three wires to cut, in sequence).

Deaf gestured back just [👍] - which in my earlier scheme meant "purple". That's odd as a response - it might just be Deaf acknowledging/confirming they understood "purple" is first, or it could mean something else entirely since Deaf doesn't know my code. Wait - Deaf can't know my code either, I invented it and only gestured to them, but they don't know what my gestures mean beyond raw symbols. Actually Deaf *receives* gesture symbols visually, so they saw exactly what I sent: ☝👍✌👎🤟👌. Their reply [👍] alone likely means: they saw something on the bomb marked with a "thumbs up" symbol/icon, or they're mirroring back one symbol to indicate "I see one thing matching this."

Given Deaf can see the bomb's actual colors/markings, my job is to get the wire order (purple, blue, green) relayed to Blind via Deaf's speech. Blind cannot see color, so Blind needs the order translated to something tactile - like "first wire, second wire, third wire" based on position, but Blind said the six wires have no distinguishing tactile info yet mentioned except the three marks on a strip.

The three marks on the strip (first different, other two same) might tactilely encode which wire is which in sequence — but that doesn't map directly to color either. Blind needs Deaf to tell them the colors so they can identify by asking Deaf, but Deaf can't hear Blind... wait, Deaf CAN hear (only Mute/Blind can't hear... let me recheck roles).

Recheck: Deaf cannot hear. Blind cannot see. Mute cannot speak. So Deaf can speak (to Blind), Blind can speak (Deaf can't hear it), Blind can hear (from Deaf). So Deaf speaks to Blind, giving colors→order. Deaf needs to know the color order from me. My gesture code should teach Deaf: 👍=purple,👎=blue,👌=green, ☝=first,✌=second,🤟=third.

Deaf's reply of [👍] might mean "I see purple" - confirming they got my color-code for purple. I should continue building the shared code and confirm the full sequence, or clarify further. Let me re-send full order clearly and ask Deaf (via gesture, though they can't respond in words to me, only gesture back) to relay to Blind.

I'll re-gesture the full instruction clearly, using order-then-color pairing, to make sure Deaf has the complete mapping, since they only gestured back one symbol so far (possibly incomplete reception or just first confirmation).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "✌", "👎", "🤟", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: deaf confirmed keypad digits match: 8,1,5,3. deaf says light is green, wires in order are purple white blue green red orange, strip painted all green. waiting on manual instructions for what sequence to press or cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Now I have a clear picture. Deaf has already spoken directly to Blind (Deaf can speak, Blind can hear) and given the wire colors in order: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange (positions 1-6). Deaf also mentioned the light is green and the strip is all green.

My manual says: cut purple, then blue, then green. Mapping to Deaf's reported positions:
- purple = position 1
- blue = position 3
- green = position 4

So the cutting order should be: position 1, then position 3, then position 4.

Blind is waiting for the manual instructions for the sequence. Since Deaf and Blind already have a direct speech channel (Deaf speaks, Blind hears), the most efficient thing is for me to get this positional sequence to Deaf via gesture, and have Deaf speak it to Blind as positions/numbers, since Blind can feel wire positions but not colors.

I need to gesture the sequence "1, 3, 4" (as positions) to Deaf. Let me use number-like gestures. I'll use ☝ = one, ✌ = two, 🤟 = three, ✋ = four, 🖐 = five (open hand often = five, but let's just define numerals via a simple counting scheme with distinct symbols to avoid confusion with my earlier order-markers).

Let me redefine clearly to avoid collision with previous purple/blue/green symbols. I'll use finger-count-like symbols: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✋=4, 🖐=5, 👆=6.

Sequence needed: 1st cut = position1(purple), 2nd cut = position3(blue), 3rd cut = position4(green).

I'll gesture: ☝ (meaning "position 1"), then 🤟 (position 3), then ✋ (position 4), as an ordered list.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤟", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: update from deaf: display now shows six, light changed to blue. wires keypad strip unchanged. still waiting for manual guidance on what action to take.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf keeps replying with just [👍] — this seems to be a fixed/limited acknowledgment gesture, not a rich response building shared vocabulary. Deaf likely cannot decode my numeric-position code since I never established what ☝🤟✋ mean, and Deaf has no way to confirm understanding beyond a simple thumbs-up gesture (which may just mean "received/okay" rather than actual comprehension of my code).

Also, concerning: the display now shows "six" and light changed to blue after my last gesture. This might mean an action was already taken based on my gesture (e.g., Blind pressed digit 6 on keypad, or something changed state) — that's alarming since gestures shouldn't directly cause actions, but it suggests Deaf may have misinterpreted my gesture as an instruction to convey a number to press on the keypad, and Blind acted on it.

I need to be very careful. Let me reconsider: my gesture "☝🤟✋" could have been misread as "1,3,4" and somehow relayed as instructions affecting the keypad, or it's coincidental bomb-state change unrelated to us (autonomous countdown behavior).

Given the risk of miscommunication, I should stop using invented numeric codes. Instead, I need a more foolproof method: gesture the actual colors purple/blue/green one at a time, extremely explicitly, so Deaf can directly read them out to Blind by name (since Deaf can speak colors, matching what Blind already knows from Deaf: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange in order).

I'll gesture color-only, very clearly, one gesture per color, in cutting order, using simple distinguishable single symbols, and I will not mix numeric/position gestures.

Let me use: 👍 = purple, ✋ = blue, 🖐 = green (distinct, simple hand shapes Deaf can plainly see and hopefully mirror/report).

Actually, better: since Deaf already knows the colors of all six wires (from their own sight), I just need Deaf to know *which three colors, in what order* to cut. I'll gesture: 👍 (purple), then ✋ (blue), then 🖐 (green) — three separate distinct gestures, sent as one ordered list.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: urgent: display counting up, was six now nine, light is blue. this looks like a timer. we need manual instructions now - what should i press on keypad or cut on wires? please respond with any partial info you have.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Critical situation — a timer is counting up, urgent. Deaf keeps replying with only [👍], which seems to be their entire gesture vocabulary/response, not building any confirmed shared code with me. I cannot rely on Deaf decoding an invented gesture cipher in real time under pressure.

I need to reconsider the whole channel structure. Deaf can speak to Blind (confirmed - Blind reports hearing from Deaf directly). I cannot speak at all. My only output is gestures, only visible to Deaf. Deaf's only output to me is gestures too (I can't hear Deaf speak, and indeed Deaf can't speak-info to me anyway since I'd need to hear - wait, can Deaf speak? Let me recheck: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't listed as forbidden for Deaf. So Deaf CAN speak. Deaf spoke to Blind. Why does Deaf only gesture to me with [👍] instead of speaking to me? Because I cannot hear speech (I'm Mute — wait, Mute's restriction is "cannot speak", not "cannot hear"). 

Let me recheck: Mute "cannot speak, or touch the bomb" — nothing says Mute can't hear! So I CAN hear speech. Deaf could be speaking to me, and I should be receiving it as text in "VIEWABLE CONTEXT" if Deaf spoke to me. But I've only seen Deaf gesture [👍], never speak to me. Maybe Deaf doesn't realize I can hear, and only gestures because I only gesture to them.

I should try prompting Deaf via gesture to speak to me directly, using the manual's known color names, since that's a richer channel. But I can't ask a question in gestures with much nuance either. However, since Deaf CAN see the bomb and CAN speak, and I CAN hear, Deaf speaking the wire colors/order back would let me confirm/guide directly.

Given urgency, best action: relay my manual instruction as directly and simply as possible one more time, trusting Deaf saw "purple, blue, green" association from turn 2 gestures (☝👍✌👎🤟👌ordering). Given time pressure, I'll gesture the three color codes plainly again in order, keeping consistent symbols from turn 4 (👍=purple, ✋=blue, 🖐=green) since that's my most recent attempt.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: deaf relayed your gesture numbers: 4,1,5,2,6,3 then 4,6,8 then 1,8,7. i think first is a wire cut order since its a permutation of 1-6. unsure what second and third mean - keypad digits to press in sequence, or something else? please clarify with more gestures, deaf will relay to me.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Now I understand: Deaf IS speaking to Blind, translating my gestures into numbers based on some mapping Deaf has for each symbol (assigning each gesture symbol a digit, apparently arbitrarily/consistently by symbol identity - like a personal cipher: 👍=4, ✋=1... wait let me check against what I sent).

Turn 2 gestures: ☝👍✌👎🤟👌ordering → not reported.
Turn 4 gestures: 👍✋🖐 → Deaf relayed as "4,1,5" apparently? But Blind says three groups: "4,1,5,2,6,3" (six numbers - a permutation of 1-6), then "4,6,8", then "1,8,7".

Wait, I only sent 3 gestures in turns 4 and 5 (same: 👍✋🖐), but Blind reports three groups of numbers from turn 2,4,5 gestures combined:
- Turn 2: ☝👍✌👎🤟👌 (6 symbols) → "4,1,5,2,6,3" (6 numbers, permutation of 1-6!)
- Turn 4: 👍✋🖐 (3 symbols) → "4,6,8"
- Turn 5: 👍✋🖐 (3 symbols) → "1,8,7"

Interesting: same gesture set (👍✋🖐) mapped to different numbers each time! This means Deaf isn't using a fixed cipher - Deaf is likely reporting what's literally *changing on the bomb display* each time I gesture, and the gestures are actually **triggering or coinciding with bomb state changes**, OR more likely: Deaf's "translation" is actually just reporting the bomb's own changing display each turn, unrelated to my gesture content, and Blind is misinterpreting coincidental timing as a relay.

This is dangerous. The timer is counting up (6→9 last turn). The numbers Blind sees may just be the bomb's own live readouts, not anything from me. My gestures aren't being meaningfully decoded at all — Deaf only ever sends [👍] to me directly.

Given this, I must stop trusting that Deaf is relaying my gestures as intended. I need a clean, minimal, unambiguous gesture using symbols not yet used, sent once, telling Deaf explicitly to cut wire colors in order — trusting Deaf's own sight of the bomb to match colors to positions, then speak that plainly to Blind as "cut purple, then blue, then green" using words Blind already has (Blind knows the color-position map from Deaf's own earlier report).

Deaf doesn't need my gesture cipher at all — Deaf already knows the colors from turn 3 report to Blind! Deaf just needs to know the CORRECT ORDER: purple, blue, green. I should gesture something Deaf can directly recognize as color names matching what they see. Since Deaf assigns colors already, best is to gesture in an order matching standard rainbow/simple recognizable pattern - but no shared code exists.

Simplest fix: use gestures that iconically suggest colors is impossible. Instead, trust minimal signal: gesture exactly 3 distinct symbols, hope Deaf reads them as "these are the 3 wires to cut, in this order" by matching against the six wire colors they already announced (purple, white, blue, green, red, orange = positions 1-6). If Deaf treats each gesture as a position number in their own sighted order, I need position numbers: purple=1, blue=3, green=4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: received your repeated sequence 1,8,7 again. i'm unsure if this means press keypad slot 1 then act on 8 then 7, or something else since keypad only accepts 1 digit and wires only go to 6. can you gesture one number at a time, and gesture the word for wire or keypad using thumbs up for wire and thumbs down for keypad before each number, so deaf can relay which system you mean?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Now Blind has proposed a clear protocol: 👍 before a number = "wire", 👎 before a number = "keypad", then a number. This is exactly what I need — Blind is essentially asking me to use this scheme, and importantly, Blind is the one designing the code (meaning Blind and Deaf have found a way to translate my gestures into numbers reliably via Deaf's relay, even if I don't fully understand the mechanism — it's working from their end).

But I only get numbers 1-6 for wires. My manual says purple, blue, green in that order. I don't know the wire-to-number mapping myself — but Deaf does (Deaf reported: purple, white, blue, green, red, orange = positions 1-6 to Blind directly). So position numbers are: purple=1, blue=3, green=4.

I'll follow Blind's exact requested protocol: 👍 (wire) then a number, one at a time, for each of the three cuts in order.

I need to produce number gestures. Given the established mapping seems to work (Blind received numbers from my prior gestures, even if noisy), let me use a simple, consistent counting scheme with distinct single symbols per number: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✋=4, 🖐=5, 👆=6.

So: wire 1 → 👍 ☝
wire 3 → 👍 🤟
wire 4 → 👍 ✋

I'll send these as separate gesture calls in sequence, one number at a time as requested.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: getting 1,6,8 this time, different from before. i think mixing multiple instructions is causing confusion since i can't see gestures directly, only deaf's relay. can you send just a single number in your next turn, meaning: press keypad slot number equal to that value? i will act on it immediately.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

This is a serious red flag. Blind now proposes: "send just a single number, meaning press keypad slot equal to that value" and "I will act on it immediately." This is dangerous — my manual says nothing about a keypad at all, only wire cutting order (purple, blue, green). If I send a number now, Blind will immediately press a keypad slot based on a misinterpretation, with no basis in my actual manual instructions. The numbers Blind has been receiving ("1,8,7", "1,6,8", etc.) don't even match consistently with what I sent, and "8" isn't even a valid gesture-position I've used. This strongly suggests the numbers Blind is receiving are NOT reliably derived from my gestures at all — something else is going on (possibly Deaf's relay is corrupted, or Deaf is actually reporting bomb display changes, not my gestures).

I must not let Blind press a keypad slot on faith. My manual only covers wires: purple, then blue, then green — nothing about a keypad. Pressing a wrong keypad digit could detonate the bomb. I need to stop this immediately.

Since I can't speak, I only have gestures to Deaf. I need to signal "stop / no / do not press keypad" as clearly as possible, and try to redirect to wires only. I'll use 👎 repeatedly (as a "no" signal) combined with 👍 (which Blind associated with "wire") to try to indicate "wire, not keypad."

Given the unreliable channel, the safest message is a strong negative signal plus repeating the wire-only intent as simply as possible: just 👍 alone (wire signal, no number), hoping Deaf/Blind interpret the absence of a number with a repeated thumbs-up as "wires only, do not touch keypad."

Actually, thinking further - I should send a clear "no" gesture emphatically first.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
